entries.name: COST Action P18
entries.background: A European-funded research collaboration proposal on the physics of lightning, bringing together researchers from about 30 countries.

entries.name: fragmented science
entries.senseHere: A description of ball lightning research as splintered into disconnected efforts, with no shared framework tying together data collection, theorizing, and laboratory testing.

entries.name: Prairie Meteorite Network
entries.background: A US program that photographed the night sky continuously for over a decade to track meteors falling to Earth, incidentally capturing other rare sky phenomena.

entries.name: Wilhelm von Haidinger
entries.background: A 19th-century Austrian geologist and mineralogist who was a member of Vienna's Imperial Academy of Sciences, known for careful scientific observation and documentation.

entries.name: Othniel Charles Marsh
entries.background: An American paleontology professor at Yale and president of the US National Academy of Sciences, famous for his fossil discoveries and rivalry with another paleontologist in the 'Bone Wars'.

entries.name: Abbott Lawrence Rotch
entries.background: An American meteorologist who founded the Blue Hill Observatory near Boston and pioneered the use of kites to measure the upper atmosphere.

entries.name: Walther Gerlach
entries.background: A German physics professor renowned for the 1922 Stern-Gerlach experiment, which demonstrated that atomic particles have quantized spin, a foundational result in quantum physics.

entries.name: Roger Clifton Jennison
entries.background: A British radio astronomer who worked at the Jodrell Bank Observatory before becoming a physics professor at the University of Kent.

entries.name: Cavendish Laboratory
entries.background: The physics research laboratory of Cambridge University, one of the world's most famous centers for discoveries in physics.

entries.name: Pikes Peak
entries.background: A 4302 m mountain in Colorado's Rocky Mountains, the highest summit in the southern Front Range, once home to a Harvard weather observation station.

entries.name: Puy de Dôme Observatory
entries.background: A scientific observatory atop a 1465 m extinct volcano in France's Massif Central, historically used for atmospheric and weather research.

entries.name: Georg Wilhelm Richmann
entries.background: A Baltic German physicist and member of the St Petersburg Academy of Sciences who died in 1753 while experimenting with atmospheric electricity using an ungrounded conductor.

entries.name: Keraunoparalysis
entries.senseHere: A short-lived paralysis or numbness in a limb caused by nearby lightning or electrical shock, distinct from lasting psychological trauma.
entries.background: The term describes a recognized medical effect of lightning strikes on the nervous system, still used by doctors today to distinguish immediate physical shock symptoms from longer-term nerve or psychological injury.

entries.name: Jean-Martin Charcot
entries.background: A French physician considered the founder of modern neurology, who taught at the University of Paris and was Sigmund Freud's teacher in the 1880s.

entries.name: Soil strike theory
aliases: Abrahamson and Dinniss soil strike theory
entries.senseHere: An explanation proposing that ball lightning forms when a lightning strike vaporizes soil minerals, creating a glowing ball of burning particles.
